summary:
ARES-1 is an interactive Mars exploration platform featuring a 3D globe built using NASA's MGS MOLA elevation data and the USGS Viking Mars colour mosaic. Users can explore Martian geography, topography, geological landmarks, and rover and orbiter locations.

Its key feature is a slope- and dust-aware route planner powered by the A* algorithm, which identifies comparatively suitable routes using terrain gradients and modelled dust conditions. Other features include elevation profiles, route comparisons, custom coordinates, GeoJSON export, geological imagery, hazard layers, and a Mars solar-time calculator.

How to Access and Use:
Download the ARES-1 ZIP folder.
Extract the folder.
Open the extracted ARES-1 Mars Radar folder.
Double-click index.html to launch the interactive Mars map in your browser.
Explore the globe, switch map layers, and use the Mars Navigator to plan routes.
An internet connection may be required for online map tiles and imagery. If the application does not open, use a local web server.
ARES-1 demonstrates how planetary data and computational algorithms can support Martian exploration and future robotic navigation.
details:
ARES-1 is an interactive Mars exploration platform that integrates NASA's MGS MOLA elevation data and USGS Viking Mars colour mosaic to create a 3D globe for exploring Martian geography, topography, and geological features.

Its key innovation is a slope- and dust-aware route-planning system powered by the A* pathfinding algorithm. It identifies comparatively suitable routes by analysing terrain gradients and modelled dust conditions. Users can explore elevation profiles, compare direct and planned distances, enter custom coordinates, and export routes in GeoJSON format.

The platform also features geological imagery, rover and orbiter visualizations, environmental hazard layers, and a Mars solar-time calculator.

Benefits and Impact: ARES-1 makes planetary data more accessible, demonstrates intelligent terrain navigation, and promotes understanding of the challenges involved in future robotic Mars exploration.

Technology Used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, A* pathfinding, NASA MOLA elevation datasets, USGS Viking imagery, and GeoJSON.

Creativity and Design Considerations: The project combines interactive planetary visualization with terrain-based route planning, considering elevation, slope, dust conditions, route distance, and accessibility to create an engaging exploration experience.

ARES-1 aims to demonstrate how scientific data and computational algorithms can contribute to future Mars exploration.
